title: Autorevert Sentinel with Cost-Fidelity Checks and Reconciliation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Config changes that tune batching, caching, or routing policies can produce sudden cost regressions or quality degradations. We need an autonomous mechanism that can safely detect harmful config effects and revert them with minimal operational overhead while preserving availability.

Goal: Build an "Autorevert Sentinel" that combines cost delta detection, fidelity checks (quality/regression signals), and state reconciliation to perform conservative automated reverts. The sentinel must: 1) run continuous post-apply monitoring for a configurable window, 2) evaluate multi-signal triggers (cost, latency, error rate, eval-prompt regressions), 3) attempt safe rollback when triggers exceed thresholds, and 4) reconcile system state to ensure eventual consistency across control planes (hosted, dedicated, private).

Scope: Proof-of-concept across hosted inference and Dedicated control plane. Includes: config-change watcher, multi-signal detector, rollback executor with canary-aware orchestration, reconciliation loop to harmonize failed partial rollbacks, and human-in-the-loop escalation for borderline cases. Excludes full on-prem packaging (follow-up).
acceptance_criteria: Sentinel observes config overlays and starts monitoring within 30s of apply
Triggers based on cost delta (>25% 95th percentile token cost over baseline) OR latency/error regressions (p99 latency +10%, error rate +3%) OR eval prompt degradation (automated tests fail >10%)
When triggers exceed thresholds, sentinel performs staged rollback: canary slice -> majority -> global, with circuit-breaker to stop if rollback worsens metrics
All rollbacks are recorded with audit metadata (operator, revert reason, snapshots) and surfaced to Console incidents/alerts
Reconciliation loop detects drift between control plane and node pools and performs idempotent repairs within 10 minutes or flags escalation
Unit and integration tests cover detector logic, rollback paths, and reconciliation idempotency with mocked backends
Runbook documented and accessible from Console with rollback transparency and rollback rationale in incident timeline
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: False positives causing unnecessary rollbacks -> Mitigation: multi-signal confirmation window and vote-based trigger (require >=2 signals or persistent single-signal over window)
Risk: Rollback flapping under noisy signals -> Mitigation: exponential backoff, cooldown windows, hysteresis on triggers
Risk: Partial rollback leaves cluster in inconsistent state -> Mitigation: reconciliation loop with idempotent operations and compensating actions
Risk: Cost detection blind spots for long-tail workloads -> Mitigation: tiered baselines by route/model and sample-weighted aggregation
implementation_notes: Detector will consume traces and metrics from observability pipeline (Grafana/Prometheus + trace spans) and evaluation results from existing eval service
Rollback executor will reuse Conductor orchestration primitives used by Deploy Service but add a 'safe-apply' mode that supports staged canary/timeout and explicit revert snapshotting
Reconciliation will be implemented as a controller that compares desired state from config-store and observed state from agent heartbeats, using optimistic locking to avoid thundering herd
We will add a cost-fidelity scoring model (simple weighted z-scores initially) to combine heterogeneous signals into a single revert confidence score
Expose primary knobs in Console: revert thresholds, emergency-off toggle, cooldown period, and notification channels
test_plan: Unit tests for detector math and scoring model
Simulated traffic tests that inject cost spikes and latency regressions while validating staged rollback behavior
Chaos test: introduce partial failure during rollback to validate reconciliation loop recovers without human intervention
E2E staging run with blue-green toggle to validate audit trail and console visibility
Runbook tabletop with on-call to validate notification cadence and escalation
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (canary): deploy sentinel in staging and one low-risk customer cohort; monitor for 2 weeks
Phase 2 (expanded): enable for 10% of production applies with read-only mode for 48h then autotriage enabled for non-blocking reverts
Phase 3 (general): enable automatic rollback for all applies with default thresholds, allow customers to opt-out per-team
Fallback: quick disable via Console emergency toggle and manual rollback playbook
